title: The Essex
wikitext:
{{Short description|American R&B vocal group}} {{Use mdy dates|date=July 2022}} '''The Essex''' was an American [[Rhythm and blues|R&B]] [[List of vocal groups|vocal group]] formed in 1962. They are best known for their 1963 song "[[Easier Said Than Done (The Essex song)|Easier Said Than Done]]". ==Career== Founding members Walter Vickers ([[guitar]]) and Rodney Taylor ([[drum]]s) were members of the [[United States Marine Corps]] stationed in [[Okinawa Island|Okinawa]], [[Japan]].{{cite web|first=Jason|last=Ankeny|url=https://www.allmusic.com/artist/the-essex-mn0000057973/biography|title=The Essex Biography|publisher=[[AllMusic]]|accessdate=4 January 2009}} After being transferred to [[Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune|Camp LeJeune]] in [[North Carolina]], they enlisted fellow Marines Billy Hill (aka Billy Proctor) and Rudolph Johnson as group members. Next they added a female lead singer, Anita Humes, another Marine. The band was signed to a [[recording contract]] in 1963 after submitting a [[demo (music)|demo]] to [[Roulette Records]]. "Easier Said Than Done" was [[songwriter|written]] by Larry Huff and William Linton. Released as the B side of their first [[single (music)|single]], the song reached the [[chart-topper|top]] of the U.S. [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] [[record chart|chart]]. The track sold over one million [[gramophone record|records]] and received a [[music recording sales certification|gold disc]] award from the [[Recording Industry Association of America|R.I.A.A.]]{{cite book|first=Joseph|last=Murrells|year=1978|title=The Book of Golden Discs|edition=2nd|publisher=Barrie and Jenkins Ltd|location=London|page= [https://archive.org/details/bookofgoldendisc00murr/page/158 158/9]|isbn=0-214-20512-6|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/bookofgoldendisc00murr/page/158}} "Easier Said Than Done" charted at No. 41 in the [[UK Singles Chart]] in August 1963.{{cite book|first=David|last=Roberts|year=2006|title=British Hit Singles & Albums|edition=19th|publisher=Guinness World Records Limited|location=London|isbn=1-904994-10-5|page=186}} Rudolph Johnson left the group, and the Essex became a quartet. Three months after "Easier Said Than Done" reached No. 1 in July 1963, the group had a No. 12 Billboard [[hit record|hit]] with the follow-up song, "A Walkin' Miracle" in September 1963. On the label of this single, the group name appeared as The Essex Featuring Anita Humes. "She's Got Everything", their next single, written by [[Jimmy Radcliffe]] and Oramay Diamond, was a Billboard No. 56 hit. Being Marines made it hard for the group to take advantage of their hits; for example, before long, Johnson was posted to Okinawa. Rodney Taylor was killed in 1966 in New York City during an attempted mugging. He was buried at Oak Hill Cemetery in Gary, Indiana. All of his former bandmates attended his funeral. Humes released several [[solo (music)|solo]] singles for Roulette, but had no chart success. She died on May 30, 2010, in [[Harrisburg, Pennsylvania]], aged 69.{{cite web|url=http://www.thedeadrockstarsclub.com/2010.html|title=The Dead Rock Stars Club January to June 2010|publisher=Thedeadrockstarsclub.com|accessdate=2015-08-18}} In the 1970s, Hill headed up a group called the Courtship. ==Band member origins== *Walter Vickers - [[New Brunswick, New Jersey|New Brunswick]], [[New Jersey]] *Rodney Taylor - [[Gary, Indiana|Gary]], [[Indiana]] *Rudolph Johnson - [[New York City|New York]] *Willie "Billy" Hill - [[Princeton, New Jersey]] *Anita Humes - [[Harrisburg, Pennsylvania|Harrisburg]], [[Pennsylvania]] ==Discography== ===Albums=== {| class="wikitable" |- !
